review_notes: Selected the principal estimated-method family from the simulation section: the repeated full-sample regression in Eq. (14) and the group-specific sample-splitting fits in Eq. (15). Earlier conceptual equations are not promoted to fitted regressions.
All nine slopes are research-interest targets because the authors explicitly evaluate inference performance across all coefficients. FRQ remains only partly operationalized in this paper.

The selected tables report simulation test-size/rejection frequencies, RMSE, and power rather than coefficient estimates and individual inference. These diagnostics are not relabeled as coefficient results.
The paper does not name the within-group estimator in Eq. (15); Eq. (14) and Eq. (15) cover multiple fixed-effect and inference settings, so no single family-wide setting is asserted.
descriptive_reason: No variable-level data summaries (means, standard deviations, percentiles, or ranges) for the retained outcome or predictors are reported. Page 37 gives variable definitions and overall sample counts; Tables 1–5 and 7 report simulation test-size/power diagnostics, and Table 6 reports coefficient-estimator RMSE. The standard-deviation discussion on page 59 concerns the simulated coefficient estimator used to define power alternatives, not a data-variable descriptive.
results_review_notes: Eq. (14) full-sample OLS and Eq. (15) group-specific sample-splitting fits are retained as the principal compared estimated-method family. Eq. (16) is supporting for the residual-based ad hoc group-selection procedure; the original additive firm/time fixed-effects fit is supporting because its estimates calibrate the simulated outcomes.
No performance-table cell is entered as a coefficient estimate: the reported values are simulation rejection frequencies, RMSE, or power.
